I will keep the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I am 62, so I want a system I know well, that sells easily, uses the machines and habits I already have, and does not ask me to take big market risks. In Quzhou, this rotation fits the climate, the irrigation conditions, and the local way of farming. I will not split the land into too many crops, because that makes field work, seed buying, fertilizing, and pest control more complicated for me. I would rather keep the whole farm in grain, aim for steady output, and manage labor carefully.

For this year, I will carry my winter wheat through the spring, then I will seed summer maize right after harvest. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, add some phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for weeds, aphids, and disease pressure. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize. I will use hybrid maize because I care about stable yield, and I will use no-tillage seeding after wheat to save time, save moisture, and reduce work. I will still fertilize, but I will keep the program straightforward and not overly heavy. My goal is not chasing the highest possible yield; it is getting a dependable crop from the full year with work I can realistically manage myself.
